name: Cannabis advertising rules
where_it_stands: Cannabis ads are governed mostly by state rules that limit placement to adult audiences and ban youth appeal, while a federal law punishes ads that help sell Schedule I drugs. That federal ad ban no longer reaches state-licensed medical marijuana after the April 2026 move to Schedule III, but Google, Meta and TikTok have not loosened their cannabis ad policies.
summary: State rules do most of the work. California lets licensees advertise only where reliable data shows at least 71.6% of the audience is 21 or older, and bans ads that depict minors, use cartoons or candy imagery, or promote free product, giveaways or contests; Colorado's Marijuana Enforcement Division rules also restrict cannabis advertising. At the federal level, 21 U.S.C. 843(c) makes it a crime to knowingly place an ad that seeks to illegally buy, sell or distribute a Schedule I substance, punishable by up to four years in prison; the Congressional Research Service notes that this penalty no longer applies to marijuana products moved to Schedule III, while adult-use marijuana stays in Schedule I. Platforms set their own rules. X became the first major social network to accept cannabis ads in US states where they are legal in February 2023. In May 2026 a digital marketer told MJBizDaily that the large platforms were open to changes but had made none, and they still bar promotional offers and product images in cannabis ads.

what_changes.text: Medical-only advertising carries less federal criminal risk after rescheduling, but state placement and content rules still apply, and adult-use ads remain tied to a Schedule I product.
Wider broadcast or platform access would lower customer acquisition costs, but platforms appear to be waiting for broader federal change.
Ads remain restricted to adult audiences, and offers such as giveaways are banned in states like California.

timeline.event: Twitter (now X) says it will allow cannabis ads in US states where they are legal
State-licensed medical marijuana moves to Schedule III, outside the federal Schedule I ad ban
MJBizDaily reports major platforms have not changed cannabis ad policies

faq.q: Can cannabis companies advertise on TV or social media?
faq.a: Platform and broadcaster policies are the main barrier. X accepts cannabis ads in legal states; Google, Meta and TikTok had not changed their restrictions as of May 2026.
California, among other states, allows cannabis ads only where at least 71.6% of the audience is reasonably expected to be 21 or older.

faq.q: Did rescheduling make cannabis ads federally legal?
faq.a: For state-licensed medical marijuana, the federal Schedule I ad penalty no longer applies. Adult-use marijuana is still Schedule I.
